themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints surged to 4 this week—a 700% spike versus the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either newly discovered hazardous materials in buildings undergoing renovation or a shift in resident reporting amid the district's heavy construction activity (1,357 DOB permits filed in 90 days, including 40 demolitions).
evidence: 4 asbestos complaints this week vs 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.0)
1,357 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, including 40 full demolitions and 150 ALT-CO permits involving demolition and reconstruction
Hazardous Materials complaints also up 167% (7 complaints last week vs 2.6 avg, z-score: 4.41)
reporting_angles: Are contractors properly managing asbestos abatement during renovation wave in Greenpoint/Williamsburg?
Interview residents near active demolition sites about health concerns and notification protocols

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 8 this week—a 146% jump from the 3.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling a potential public health or sanitation infrastructure issue that coincides with rising encampment complaints (22 last week, up 283%) and hazmat concerns.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints this week vs 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.96)
Encampment complaints also spiked to 22 last week (up 283% from 5.8 avg), suggesting potential correlation with homelessness-related sanitation
Community board has repeatedly requested homeless services and DEP capital funding, indicating unresolved systemic issue
reporting_angles: Are sanitation services overwhelmed by volume, or is there a new source (pest infestation, wildlife migration)?
Document the overlap between encampment locations and dead animal complaints

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from residential sources jumped to 223 this week—a 39% spike above the 160.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—marking a sustained escalation in a category that already dominates the district's 311 volume and reflects ongoing quality-of-life pressure amid development activity.
evidence: 223 residential noise complaints this week vs 160.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.11)
Noise accounts for 4,909 of 14,069 total complaints (35% of all complaints); residential noise is largest single category
Community board repeatedly requests 'Improve traffic and pedestrian safety, including traffic calming' from DOT, suggesting noise linked to vehicle activity and development
reporting_angles: Which neighborhoods within Greenpoint/Williamsburg are noise hotspots, and are they clustered near active construction sites?
Interview residents about whether noise is from nightlife, construction, or delivery traffic; what enforcement gaps exist?

themes_detail.label: Construction & Plumbing Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: General Construction/Plumbing complaints rose to 42 last week—a 73% increase from the 24.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—suggesting either improper contractor practices or residents reporting inadequate oversight of the 1,357 active DOB permits (773 alterations) flooding the district.
evidence: 42 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs 24.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.8)
773 alteration permits filed in last 90 days; 220 new building permits; asbestos and hazmat complaints also spiking simultaneously
Community board has made standing requests for 'Other expense request for DOB' and 'Land use planning, technical and urban design support,' indicating oversight capacity concerns
reporting_angles: Are DOB inspectors keeping pace with permit volume, or are contractors cutting corners?
Investigate complaints against specific developers or contractors involved in major rezonings (200 Kent, 20 Berry, 289 Kent)

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Homelessness Pressure
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 22 last week—a 283% spike from the 5.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—indicating accelerating street homelessness that the district's repeated requests for DHS funding have failed to address and that correlates with dead animal, sanitation, and hazmat spikes.
evidence: 22 encampment complaints last week vs 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.43)
Community board has made standing annual request for 'Other request for services for the homeless (Agency: Department of Homeless Services)'—same ask for years suggests no systemic improvement
Encampment spike correlates with dead animal (8 this week, +146%), hazmat (7 last week, +167%), and abandoned bike complaints (12 last week, +269%)
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations and interview unhoused residents about services access and barriers
Interview CB members about why annual DHS requests have not yielded results; is there a service gap in Greenpoint/Williamsburg?
